phenotype_specificity.statement: Person: early-onset IBD-like gut ulceration, gastritis and oral ulcers. Family history and initial diagnosis are 'NA'. The paper reports no exclusion of other causes for this patient. Cohort-level: most non-PGIMER centres used commercial targeted NGS panels with Sanger confirmation, and inclusion needed molecular confirmation of a monogenic SAID.

quotes.quote: Patient 41 had also presented with early onset inflammatory bowel disease and oral ulcers and a novel variant in TNFAIP3) gene was found.
Molecular analysis in most patients at other centers was carried out at commercial laboratories that use targeted gene panel by Next Generation Sequencing (NGS) techniques.
In the present study all patients who fulfilled ESID working group definition and had molecular confirmation of monogenic SAID were included.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Two-nucleotide deletion predicted to cause a frameshift (p.(Gly440ArgfsTer4)). The paper's A20 section makes no mechanism statement.

concerns: The paper writes c.1316_1317del, but the batch record is c.1318_1319del. The protein change matches (p.Gly440ArgfsTer4), so this is probably the same deletion written at a different position in a repeat. The panel should confirm.
The paper does not state a transcript.
Evidence is only a table row and one sentence. There is no case narrative, no family testing and no clinical follow-up ('NA').
The study's methods exclude infantile IBD, yet the text describes this boy as early-onset IBD. The paper does not explain this.
notes_for_panel: Thin evidence: one person, table-level data only. Family history is recorded as 'NA'.
